title: Beyond the 956: Anthony Clark, star of CBS sitcom “Yes, Dear,” dies at 62
excerpt: Anthony Clark, the comedian and actor best known as Greg Warner on the CBS sitcom “Yes, Dear,” died November 10, 2026. He was 62.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Anthony Clark, the comedian and actor best known as Greg Warner on the CBS sitcom Yes, Dear, has died at 62.

Clark died Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Deadline reported he died from complications relating to pneumonia. His death was announced Wednesday by his friend and Yes, Dear co-star Mike O'Malley, who shared a tribute on social media. The Hollywood Reporter, People and Page Six reported his death.

Born April 4, 1964, in Lynchburg, Virginia, Clark graduated from Emerson College in 1986 and began his career as a stand-up comedian before moving into acting.

He became a familiar face on network television in the 1990s with roles on NBC's Boston Common and CBS's Soul Man. His best-known role came in 2000, when he was cast as Greg Warner on Yes, Dear, the CBS comedy about two couples living under one roof. He starred on the show for six seasons, through 2006.

On film, Clark appeared in The Thing Called Love and had a memorable turn in Michael Bay's 1996 action hit The Rock, playing a flamboyant hairdresser who cuts Sean Connery's hair.

Rest in Peace, Anthony Clark.

Sources: Deadline; The Hollywood Reporter; People; Page Six.
